ideas.title: The pig lights the lamp
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: Its strength is a chain of real physics, from the induced EMF to I²R heating to Planck glow, ending in a traced emissive colour that the creature's effort drives live. That is light a game engine cannot fake. But a glowing thing has already been shown with the hot glass, and the player's part (rewinding a coil) is one dial tucked behind a friend running on a wheel, so it sits on the edge of the handmade goal rather than inside it.

ideas.title: Logs of four woods
same_form: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: This is the logs film again with density swapped in for cross-section: the same fixed watch of bodies settling side by side and the same payoff. The sinking ebony log and the grain textures are small additions. Choosing the wood at the carving spot is a real step for the boat, but the film shows nothing the last one didn't.

ideas.title: Wind a coil with your beak
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Turns that are counted from the wound path, and a Biot-Savart field that pulls particle sand, make a direct cause chain where the player's work decides the force. That fits the goal well. It is still the third wire-bench step in a row, and a tuft of sand jumping onto a nail is a modest picture.

ideas.title: The motor on the wire bench
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This mostly wires the last two posts together and fixes a camera and a key card. Anyone who saw the spinning wires has already seen the payoff. Letting the player rebend the wire and rerun it is the playable part the earlier film lacked, but it is plumbing more than something new.

ideas.title: The potter's wheel in Jump in
ideas.critique: This is the closest any idea comes to the big goal's core: in one sitting the player makes a pot, and the existing glaze flow finds their cuts. The jar itself has already been posted, so the film's payoff is half known. A mouse-drawn lathe profile is the plainest kind of 'shaping', and how real the hands on the clay will be is unclear.

ideas.title: Ring the stone you chipped
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Solved modes of a chipped stone, heard on the soundtrack, is a post the island has already made, and the lantern before it did the same with notes. A chime rack played by the friends adds an interaction, but the physics and the payoff are a repeat.

ideas.title: Paper boat race
ideas.critique: Paper that soaks up water and gets heavier over time is a new mechanism, and a race with the friends gives players a reason to come back. But floating and listing is the logs result again, and 'how they folded it' is vague enough that the likely version is a handful of preset folds.

ideas.title: A rope bridge the friends cross
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Rods for rope and rigid planks that sag under the friends' own mass would be a new kind of structure on the island, and watching a heavy friend creak across it is fun. But bridge builders are a well-worn genre, and it reaches the handmade-material goal only loosely.

ideas.title: Glass lens burns a mark
ideas.critique: The path tracer itself finding the caustic focus through a lens the player shaped, and that energy leaving a char that stays, is exactly what a game engine cannot do. It is strong. Blowing and grinding the lens is a lot of work stacked up front, and the risk is that the lens ends up as a preset curve.

ideas.title: A paper glider that flies by its own folds
ideas.critique: A vortex-lattice model over the folded mesh, so that the creases alone decide the flight, is new aerodynamics on the island, and the fold-throw-refold loop is a game people return to. A thrown object filmed in flight has been posted before with the boomerang, and the whole idea hinges on the folds really being the player's own.
